summary: One pull request in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc with three parts. A: visibleMarks (marks.go) returns nil when no rendered mark is present, otherwise a fresh slice sorted with slices.SortFunc only when it holds 2+ marks; renderedMarkTypes stays the one list. B: asWritten (render.go) becomes one copy-on-write pass that returns the input node when nothing under it changes (strip anchor marks, merge adjacent equal-mark text, writtenLineBreaks for textblocks that need it, U+0000 replacement with cloned Attrs only on the nodes that hold one); writeLineBreaksIn and writeNulsAsReplacement are deleted; StripAnchorMarks keeps its deep-copy contract. C: emphasisParser.Parse sets a per-parse parser.Context key when the final canOpen/canClose differ between the two rule sets; the renderer reads a run back with flankingOnlyMarkdown only when the first read-back passes and that key is set; inlineSignature(nodes) and referencedLabels(nodes) computed once per inlineWithEscapes. Planner's profile of RenderWithBlockOffsets on four real LINUX specs: read-back 25%, asWritten 24%, visibleMarks 25%, Validate 5% of render CPU; prototypes cut allocation about 65-70% and render time about 45-50%, output byte-identical.
tasks: 1. bun install --frozen-lockfile at the repository root; cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/... -count=1 at base, keep the failure list.
3. B in pmdoc/render.go: new copy-on-write asWritten, delete writeLineBreaksIn and writeNulsAsReplacement, rewrite the asWritten, NUL and Render doc comments.
4. C in pmdoc/emphasis.go, pmdoc/parse.go, pmdoc/render_inline.go (both read-back call pairs, render_inline.go:117-118 and 141-142).

5. Permanent tests: render_written_test.go (oracle of today's StripAnchorMarks+writeLineBreaksIn+writeNulsAsReplacement vs new asWritten on generated branch cases and real-size corpus-built documents with deterministic anchors, line feeds and isInline hardbreaks, compared by rendering and JSON()); input tree unchanged after Render, RenderWithBlockOffsets, ReadBack, NewMisread, RefuseMisreadDocument; writtenMarks leaves a [link, strong] bare-URL node's Marks unchanged; FuzzFlankingDivergence with seeds \**x, b_*a**, ***a.**** b*, a_b*a_b*, **[a](u)**_b_ (run -fuzztime 5m once).

6. Throwaway proof over every LINUX issue's current spec (dispatch issues --project LINUX --all; dispatch doc-read per issue; JSONL under $TMPDIR): gen/differential.sh --base <base> --head <head> --corpus <jsonl> prints zero for every gate; a throwaway Go test built at base and head writes markdown, offsets and NewMisread/RefuseMisreadDocument strings for parsed and anchor-bearing variants, byte-identical across the two builds. Nothing of it is committed.
7. Throwaway benchmark for r (head render time / base render time over the LINUX corpus, -benchtime 20x -count 5, medians), per part A, A+B, A+B+C; CPU and allocation profiles of the head render.

8. Load-test legs from branch legion/INFRA-639 (Dispatch built from base and from head, CPU-seconds over the window): write leg on LINUX's replay, read leg on run-step.sh --events 4 --sessions 400 --requests 60 with the default route mix routes-2026-10-26-1719Z.txt, three runs per side each; memory check on heap.pprof in-use. If INFRA-639's branch does not carry the replay yet, tell the architect and wait; substitute nothing.
9. Simplify pass; pull request with 'Dispatch: INFRA-653', the equivalence proof, the six runs per leg, spread, G, S_base, S_head, commands and inputs; CI green.

decisions.reason: Every exported render entry point refuses an invalid tree through it; removing it needs every caller's tree proven validated, reaching docs/read_cache.go and docs/mutation.go (INFRA-649's files), and is the fix ranking's F5, which no child of INFRA-512 lists. Named to the architect.

decisions.reason: The fix ranking's X9-F1 used that reading for 'all 1,157 specs'; LINUX content is not committed because the repository is public.

decisions.decision: 'Uses less CPU' is Dispatch's CPU-seconds over the measured window.
decisions.reason: INFRA-639's acceptance 9 (added by the architect) defines the per-run summary that way.

decisions.decision: Read leg keeps writes on (the 1x step's shape).
decisions.reason: The read cache (256 MiB, docs/read_cache.go:58-60) holds the whole seed, so a cold-read fold, where R8's render runs, happens only after a write moves a spec's head.
